title: Precise synthesis of targeted noble metal-based high-entropy alloy nanomaterials.

recollection.starting_material: guess: an equimolar mixture of soluble noble-metal precursors (for example, Au3+, Pt2+, Pd2+, Rh3+, Ru3+ in aqueous or organic solvent)
recollection.intervention: guess: a colloidal or micelle-templated reduction process under precisely controlled temperature and reduction-rate conditions (for example, rapid NaBH4 or CO reduction in the presence of surfactants)
recollection.structure: guess: monodisperse high-entropy alloy nanoparticles ~5–10 nm in diameter with a single-phase face-centered-cubic lattice and uniform distribution of all five noble metals
recollection.mechanism: guess: kinetically controlled simultaneous nucleation and growth of all metal species leading to a homogenous solid-solution via rapid co-reduction, with surfactant-mediated stabilization preventing phase segregation
recollection.results: guess: achieved alloy NPs with narrow size distribution (5 ± 1 nm), atomic composition within ±2 at.% of target ratios, and enhanced catalytic activity—mass activity ~1.0–1.5 A mg_metal^–1 for oxygen reduction reaction at 0.9 V vs. RHE and stability over 10,000 cycles with <10% loss

score.note: The recollection explicitly guesses a different synthesis route, morphology, mechanism, and catalytic test. The paper used spray-drying followed by H2 thermal decomposition/reduction to form porous 3D nanoframeworks with composition-dependent fcc/hcp structures, not surfactant-stabilized 5–10 nm colloidal fcc particles. Its mechanism involved sequential noble-metal reduction and H-mediated reduction/incorporation of other metals, plus thermally activated Pt–Ru fcc-to-hcp conversion. The recalled size, composition tolerance, ORR activity, and cycling figures do not match the reported MOR activity (2637 mA/mgPt), ECSA (104.4 m2/gPt), or phase-transition temperatures.
